ship.name: Columbia
ship.builder: North American Interstellar Compact (NAIC): the US, Canada and Mexico, the Great Lakes states and provinces, and a consortium of companies; European Space Agency engineers designed the drive and the rotation bearings
ship.built_where: high lunar orbit (Earth-Moon L2 yard), inside a metal-rich near-Earth asteroid (the Rock) towed there and hollowed out to take it; lunar material for the rest
ship.form: a single rotating cylinder with end caps, turning inside the Rock on its bearings; land on the inner surface; the Spindle (a fixed central cylinder) along the axis, the Sunline on its skin
ship.rock: the Rock: about 7.6 km across and 9.4 km long, 200-500 m of rock round the cavity; it does not turn; shield, quarry and mount for the Drive and the Port (bible industry: the_rock)
ship.spindle: the Spindle: the central cylinder, 200 m across (radius 100 m), from cap to cap; it does not turn; the great factories inside, fed with ore through the end-cap hubs; closed to people since the Second Lockdown (VY 178) (bible industry: the_spindle)
ship.gravity_rule: gravity falls with height toward the axis (0 g at the axis); hills feel lighter at the top; thrown balls curve spinward/antispinward (Coriolis)
ship.sky: the far side of the world is 6 km overhead, seen through haze by day; the Sunline hides it at noon
ship.sunline: a light and heat source strung along the axis (the Sunline); it brightens at dawn and dims at dusk on a 24-hour cycle; its colour and warmth follow the seasons

ends.north: the bow cap: the North Sea against a cliff wall; the Port at the axis above it (closed to people since VY 92, the First Lockdown)
ends.south: the stern cap: the South Sea against a cliff wall; the Drive and the main reactors behind it (closed since VY 92)

ship.undercroft: three decks between the floor and the hull: water stores, air plants, hydroponic and vat farms, recycling, fabricators, power conduits, the tenders' galleries and the old archives. Its outer galleries closed to people since VY 178, the whole of it since VY 271 (the Third Lockdown), except the Chutes (distribution depots), the Drops and the Return halls
ship.hull: about 12 m of regolith and water shielding outside the Undercroft; then the bearing gap; then the Rock
ship.propulsion: fusion drive at the stern: boost VY 0-31, coast VY 31-1469, brake VY 1469-1500

voyage.to: Hesper, the second planet of Alpha Centauri A (Rigil Kentaurus)

destination_facts.star: Alpha Centauri A: G2V, 1.51 x the Sun's light; companion B (K1V) and far Proxima
destination_facts.planet: Hesper: 0.92 Earth masses, 1.23 AU from A, a 1.6-Earth-year orbit, oceans and two continents, oxygen detected in 2181 (the Hesperus array); unconfirmed life
destination_facts.named: by the Compact in 2198 for the evening star (Hesperus)

voyage.what_people_know_now: most know the ship is 'going somewhere' and 'left Earth a long time ago'; few could name Hesper or Alpha Centauri; fewer know the voyage is a third done; the Steward's Launch Day 2752 Notice (VOYAGE ONE THIRD COMPLETE) is the talk of the spring

steward.name: the Steward
steward.formal: Habitat Autonomy System (HAS), node designation STEWARD
does: the Drops (raw materials and tools for people)
the boards (vehicle platforms) and the Thirty-Two (processors)
steward.tenders: small maintenance machines that work mostly at night; people leave them be (it's bad luck to block one)
steward.speaks: almost never: brief lines on the public boards (the Notices), one with each lockdown. It stopped speaking to people at the Fourth Lockdown (the Lockout, VY 350, after the Lantern); before VY 500 its last Notice was THE FLOOR IS SET. NOTHING MORE WILL BE TAKEN
steward.limits: since the Fourth Lockdown it makes for people only what the Floor allows: materials, tools, boards, the Thirty-Two (32-bit processors of early-2000s power) and few screens: enough to live well, never enough to build a mind that could challenge it or to harm the ship (bible industry: TECH_LIMITS)
steward.duty: the mission and the lives aboard. It is bound to prevent death, and every lockdown costs lives, so it locks down only as a last resort, when people's capacity for harm threatens the ship itself; never as punishment. It spaces them a generation or more apart, because two shocks in one lifetime would break the people

lockdowns.what: the Port and the Drive closed to people
the hull galleries, the end-cap hubs and the Spindle closed: people confined to the habitat and the Undercroft's inner decks
the Undercroft sealed; the Regression: goods back to the late 21st century (about 3,200 deaths in the decade after)
the Steward falls silent and sets the Floor (the Thirty-Two): a level people can hold for the rest of the voyage, so no further regression is needed; phased over ten years

people_think_of_lockdowns: 'the Steward locked the door because we were naughty' (children; wrong: none was a punishment)
'it protects the ship from us' (the College)
'it's waiting for us to grow up' (the Wardens' Library circle)
people_think: it's just the station, like weather
someone's running it from the Port (a rumour)

calendar.reckoning: VY (Voyage Year) counted from launch; official since the VY 60 Charter revision; AD kept by the churches and by old families ('the year of Our Lord 2752')
calendar.months: the Gregorian months and weeks, kept from launch
calendar.day: 24 hours by the Sunline: full light 06:00-18:00, dawn and dusk an hour or more

seasons.winter: Dec-Feb: cool, short light, frost some nights; no snow since VY 212 (the Last Snow)

calendar.present_date: 2752-05-24 (a Wednesday, VY 500); the game opens here

directions.north: toward the bow (the North Sea); the way the ship travels ('north is where we're going')
directions.spinward: the way the land turns (the direction of rotation)
directions.overhead / the Far Side: the land across the axis, 6 km up

regions.name: the North Shore
regions.what: the coast of the North Sea: harbours, beaches, headlands

regions.name: the Northland
regions.what: farms and towns between the North Shore and the Kettle

regions.name: the Kettle Valley
regions.what: the Kettle River and Lake Tamsin, round the middle of the world

regions.name: the Southland
regions.what: farms and towns between the Kettle and the South Shore

regions.name: the South Shore
regions.what: the coast of the South Sea: resort cities and cannery towns

waters.name: the North Sea
waters.what: 1 km wide, round the whole bow end; cold, clear, fished

waters.name: the South Sea
waters.what: 1 km wide, round the stern end; warmer, resort water

waters.name: the Kettle River
waters.what: 0.5 km wide, circling the world in a wide basin; ships, barges, the Falls at Harrow Falls

waters.name: Lake Tamsin
waters.what: the widening of the Kettle: named for Tamsin Okafor-Reyes, the first child born aboard

roads: US 30 (the old road names were kept from the founders' Great Lakes)
geography.rail: the Ring Line: one electric railway round the world with 146 level crossings
geography.wildlife: birds (sparrows, robins, swallows, herons, gulls, terns, wrens, larks, starlings), fish (perch, walleye, whitefish, bass, cod and haddock in the North Sea, snapper in the South), bees, rabbits, squirrels, frogs, turtles; no deer, no predators larger than a fox (the foxes were a VY 190 mistake)
geography.livestock: dairy cattle (small herds), pigs, chickens, sheep, goats; horses are few and prized

charter.name: the Charter of Columbia
clauses: the Balance (art. 3: the population shall be kept within the station's means)
the Quiet Clause (art. 21, VY 280: no person or body shall seek to alter the course or purpose of the voyage)

assembly.name: the Assembly
assembly.head: the Moderator (chosen by the Assembly for five years)

registry.name: the Registry Office
registry.seat: Kessler, with a branch in every town

shares.what: every person holds one birth share at 18; a child needs two shares (usually the parents'); shares may be gifted, pooled or bequeathed, never sold (sale is a crime since VY 466)
shares.effect: about two children per couple; childless people often gift their share to a sibling or friend; big families are built from gifted shares
words: share-kin (the children a gifted share made possible)

marshals.name: the Marshals Service
marshals.what: station police and rescue; a Marshal-General in Kessler; town constables under it

courts.name: the Station Court (Kessler) and town magistrates

draw.name: the Draw
draw.what: the monthly allotment: food credit, a home, air, water, power, clothing stock; nobody is homeless or hungry; money buys everything else

chutes.name: the Chutes
chutes.what: distribution depots where the Steward's goods stock rises from the Undercroft; shops and works buy from them

drops.name: the Drops
drops.what: fenced yards over floor hatches where the Steward's machines leave raw materials (scrap, ingots, minerals such as sulfur and ores) and basic tools for people to work; the three Board Drops are the vehicle works' yards (bible industry: DROPS; to be detailed)

board_office.name: the Board Office
board_office.what: the Assembly's office (VY 362) that counts the Steward's board allotments and audits the three works' yards

panel_board.name: the Panel Board
panel_board.what: the Assembly's board that rations the Steward's few LCD panels: hospitals first, cars never

return_halls.name: the Return halls
return_halls.what: where the dead are given back to the soil cycle; one per town

schools.what: a school in every town; the Columbia College at Bellhaven (founded VY 150 as the Wardens' College)

wire.name: the Wire
wire.what: the station network: radio, the Wire screens, town papers, the Boards (public notice screens)

faiths_2752.name: the Lakes Union Church (mainline Protestant union of VY 140)
the Freedom Baptist Convention (the Black church tradition)
the Waymakers (the voyage as pilgrimage; founded VY 455)
Muslim (the Carrow Masjid and three others)
the Plain churches (Amish and Mennonite descended; Tamarack and the Southland farms)

languages_2752.name: Columbian English
languages_2752.what: descended from Inland Northern English (the Great Lakes) mixed with the refuge's Southern and Latino Englishes

languages_2752.name: Lake Spanish
languages_2752.where: the South Shore (Playa Verde, Solana Point, Pelican Cove) and families everywhere

languages_2752.name: Carrow French
languages_2752.where: Port Carrow's Côte quarter; mostly songs, prayers and grandmothers

languages_2752.name: heritage and liturgical tongues
languages_2752.what: Latin, Polish hymns, Arabic, Hebrew, Punjabi, Hindi, Vietnamese, Anishinaabemowin words: kept by faith and family, rarely spoken whole

knowledge_levels._about: How widely something is known in 2752 (per event: share of adults who know the gist / the detail)
knowledge_levels.living: within living memory (VY 420+): people remember it or their parents told them
knowledge_levels.family: family stories: known in the families concerned, patchy elsewhere
knowledge_levels.schooled: taught in school: names and dates, little feeling
knowledge_levels.ritual: kept by a holiday, a song or a church: known as a story, not as history
knowledge_levels.place: survives as a place name or a monument; few know why
knowledge_levels.scholar: known only to Bellhaven scholars and the Wardens' Library circle
knowledge_levels.lost: known to no one (the engine may reveal it)

memory_model: The 'floating gap' of oral history (Vansina, Oral Tradition as History, 1985): people know their origins as legend and the last three generations (~80-100 years, Assmann's communicative memory) as lived; the middle centuries blur. Here: the founding (VY 0-40) is legend and ritual; VY 40-420 is thin (a few schooled names, place names); VY 420-500 is living memory.
